licenses.text:
Émile Zola, Germinal, translated by Havelock Ellis.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/emile-zola/germinal/havelock-ellis

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Émile Zola, the author, died 1902 (Wikidata Q504, P570 1902-09-29).
- Havelock Ellis, the translator and writer of the introduction or preface, died 1939 (Wikidata Q552983, P570 1939-07-08).

First publication of the text used: 1894, the English translation by Havelock Ellis. The French original was published in 1885. The country of first publication of the translation is not stated in the facts. (SE colophon: 'Germinal was published in 1885 by Émile Zola. It was translated from French in 1894 by Havelock Ellis.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the translation was first published in 1894 and the original in 1885, both before 1931, so the text is in the United States public domain. The edition's rights statement quoted below says the same.
- Country of origin: Two layers, checked separately. Original: French work by Émile Zola (died 1902), first published 1885. The author died before 1926, so the original is public domain in every country. Translation (English): the possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Each has a term of life + 70 years or less. The translator Havelock Ellis (died 1939) left the public domain in each of them on 1 January 2010, so the translation is public domain in each. The country of first publication therefore makes no difference. Havelock Ellis died after 1937, but the French wartime extension matters only when France is a possible country of first publication; the translation is in English, so France is not one of its possible countries.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon of this edition (https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/emile-zola/germinal/havelock-ellis): quoted above.
- Wikidata Q504 (Émile Zola), P570 1902-09-29.
